CHAPTER 1.2 · LEARNING AREA 1

CHAPTER 1.2 · LEARNING AREA 1 · SEPTEMBER · OCTOBER

Periodic processes and the sine function

Ebb and flow, the Ferris wheel, your own heartbeat, the length of the day: many things repeat themselves at fixed intervals. You learn to describe such periodic processes with period, amplitude and mean level, measure angles in radians and build suitable models from the sine function.

10 LESSONS3 UNITS3 LABSNATURE AND TECHNOLOGY
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • recognise periodic processes and read off period, frequency, amplitude and mean level from measured curves
  • give angles in degrees and in radians and convert between them
  • understand the graph and the properties of the sine function starting from the unit circle
  • know the effect of the parameters in $f(x) = a \cdot \sin(b(x - c)) + d$ and set up the matching function for a measured curve
CHECK-IN: CAN YOU ALREADY DO THIS?

How long is the circumference of a circle with radius 1 (to two decimal places)?

$C = 2\pi r = 2\pi \approx 6.28$

What is $\sin 30^\circ$?

$\sin 30^\circ = \tfrac12$

In a right-angled triangle the side opposite $\alpha$ is 3 cm long and the hypotenuse 5 cm. What is $\sin\alpha$?

$\sin\alpha = \tfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$

What is the angle of a quarter circle?

$\tfrac14 \cdot 360^\circ = 90^\circ$

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Periodic processes

Between the high waters at the port there are 12 hours and 25 minutes each time. After that the course of the water level repeats itself. Low water lies roughly in the middle, about 6 hours after high water.

KEY POINT · PERIODIC PROCESSES

A process is called periodic if its course repeats itself after a fixed time $p$: $f(t + p) = f(t)$ for all $t$. The smallest such $p > 0$ is the period.

The frequency $f = \tfrac1p$ says how many periods fit into one unit of time. The unit for “per second” is the hertz (Hz).

Mean level $= \tfrac{\text{largest value} + \text{smallest value}}{2}$ · amplitude $= \tfrac{\text{largest value} - \text{smallest value}}{2}$, the largest deviation from the mean level.

Periodic does not mean wave-shaped: an ECG repeats itself, but looks quite different from a smooth wave.

Measuring the period: better over several periods and then divide; that evens out measurement errors.

INTERACTIVE · ANALYSING MEASURED CURVES

Drag the two markers onto two neighbouring peaks. The largest and the smallest value are dashed, the mean level is violet.

EXAMPLE 1 · THE FERRIS WHEEL

A gondola is at most 52 m and at least 2 m high, and one turn takes 20 minutes. Find the mean level, amplitude, period and frequency.

Mean level $\tfrac{52 + 2}{2} = 27$ m, amplitude $\tfrac{52 - 2}{2} = 25$ m, period 20 min.

Frequency $\tfrac{1}{20}$ per minute, that is 3 turns per hour.

EXAMPLE 2 · THE PULSE

In the ECG the high spikes are 0.8 s apart. How high is the pulse, and what is the frequency?

In one minute $\tfrac{60}{0.8} = 75$ heartbeats fit.

Frequency $f = \tfrac{1}{0.8\text{ s}} = $ $1.25$ Hz, pulse 75 per minute.

EXERCISES

Which processes are periodic? a) the length of the day over the years   b) the water level in a bath while it fills   c) the pendulum of a grandfather clock   d) a bank balance with compound interest   e) the phases of the moon

Periodic: a), c) and e). Not periodic: b) and d); nothing repeats itself there.

In a model the maxima of solar activity are 11 years apart, and one was in 2014. When are the next two in the model?

2025 and 2036.

The water level at a tide gauge varies between −1.6 m and +1.5 m about the mean level, and the period is 12 h 25 min. Find the mean level and the amplitude. How many high waters are there per day?

Mean level $\tfrac{1.5 + (-1.6)}{2} = -0.05$ m, amplitude $\tfrac{1.5 - (-1.6)}{2} = 1.55$ m. $\tfrac{24}{12.42} \approx 1.93$, so two on most days.

A pendulum swings to and fro 20 times in 36 seconds. Find the period and the frequency.

$p = \tfrac{36}{20} = 1.8$ s, $f = \tfrac{1}{1.8} \approx 0.56$ Hz.

On Monday high water is at 5:12, and the period is 12 h 25 min. When is the first high water on Wednesday? Roughly when is the first low water on Wednesday?

Continue high water by high water: 17:37, then Tuesday …

Mon 5:12, 17:37 · Tue 6:02, 18:27 · Wed 6:52. Low water comes half a period, so a good 6 hours, after high water: Tuesday 18:27 plus 6 h 12 min gives Wednesday at about 0:40.

TEST YOURSELF!

A gondola is at most 52 m and at least 2 m high. What is the amplitude?

$\tfrac{52 - 2}{2} = 25$ m

The period of a heartbeat is 0.8 s. How high is the pulse per minute?

$\tfrac{60}{0.8} = 75$

Which frequency belongs to the period 0.5 s?

$f = \tfrac{1}{0.5\text{ s}} = 2$ Hz

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2The sine function

A point runs anticlockwise round the unit circle (radius 1). Its height above the $x$-axis is $\sin\alpha$, its distance to the right of the $y$-axis $\cos\alpha$. In the right-angled triangle this only worked up to $90^\circ$; on the circle it goes on and on: beyond $180^\circ$ the sine becomes negative, and after $360^\circ$ everything repeats itself.

For functions you prefer to measure the angle as a length: as the arc that the point travels along the unit circle. One full turn is then $2\pi \approx 6.28$ long.

KEY POINT · RADIANS AND THE SINE FUNCTION

Radians: $x = \tfrac{\alpha}{180^\circ} \cdot \pi$. So $360^\circ = 2\pi$, $180^\circ = \pi$, $90^\circ = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$, and $1 \approx 57.3^\circ$.

The sine function $f(x) = \sin x$ is defined for all real numbers, its values lie between $-1$ and $1$, and its period is $2\pi$.

Zeros at $0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \ldots$ · maxima at $\tfrac{\pi}{2} + k \cdot 2\pi$ · minima at $\tfrac{3\pi}{2} + k \cdot 2\pi$ ($k$ an integer)

The graph is point-symmetric about the origin: $\sin(-x) = -\sin x$. The cosine function is the sine curve shifted to the left by $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$: $\cos x = \sin\left(x + \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

Calculator: for degrees it is set to DEG, for radians to RAD. The most common source of errors in this chapter!

Values to remember: $\sin 30^\circ = \tfrac12$, $\sin 45^\circ = \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$, $\sin 60^\circ = \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, $\sin 90^\circ = 1$.

INTERACTIVE · FROM THE UNIT CIRCLE TO THE SINE CURVE

Turn the angle or play the motion. The orange line is the sine, the blue one the cosine.

EXAMPLE 3 · CONVERTING

Convert $45^\circ$ and $120^\circ$ into radians, and $x = 2.5$ into degrees.

$45^\circ = \tfrac{45}{180}\pi = \tfrac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785$; $120^\circ = \tfrac{2\pi}{3} \approx 2.094$

$\alpha = \tfrac{2.5}{\pi} \cdot 180^\circ \approx$ $143.2^\circ$

EXAMPLE 4 · TWO SOLUTIONS

For which $x$ between $0$ and $2\pi$ is $\sin x = 0.5$?

$\sin\tfrac{\pi}{6} = 0.5$. Between $0$ and $\pi$ the sine curve is symmetric about $x = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{6}$ works as well.

$x_1 = \tfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $x_2 = \tfrac{5\pi}{6}$, in degrees $30^\circ$ and $150^\circ$.

EXERCISES

Give in radians as a multiple of $\pi$: $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $135^\circ$, $270^\circ$, $360^\circ$.

$\tfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\tfrac{\pi}{3}$, $\tfrac{3\pi}{4}$, $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$

Give in degrees: $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\tfrac{\pi}{5}$, $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $1$, $4$.

$90^\circ$, $36^\circ$, $270^\circ$, $\approx 57.3^\circ$, $\approx 229.2^\circ$

Without a calculator, using the unit circle: $\sin\pi$, $\sin\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $\sin\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\sin\tfrac{5\pi}{2}$, $\cos\pi$.

$0$, $-1$, $-1$, $1$ (one turn more than $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$), $-1$

Solve in the interval $[0, 2\pi]$: a) $\sin x = 0.8$ (with the graphing calculator)   b) $\sin x = -0.5$

The graphing calculator gives only one solution. You find the second one with the symmetry of the curve.

a) $x_1 \approx 0.927$, $x_2 = \pi - 0.927 \approx 2.214$   b) $x_1 = \tfrac{7\pi}{6} \approx 3.665$, $x_2 = \tfrac{11\pi}{6} \approx 5.760$

On a circle with radius $r$ the angle $x$ (in radians) belongs to the arc $b = r \cdot x$. A gondola of the Ferris wheel ($r = 25$ m) goes once round. How long is its path? Which angle belongs to 10 m of path?

$2\pi \cdot 25 \approx 157.1$ m. $x = \tfrac{10}{25} = 0.4$, in degrees about $22.9^\circ$.

TEST YOURSELF!

Give $90^\circ$ in radians as a decimal to three decimal places.

$\tfrac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.571$

Calculate $\sin\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$.

Lowest point of the unit circle: $-1$

What is the period of the sine function in radians?

One full turn of the unit circle: $2\pi$

UNIT 32 LESSONS

3Parameters of the sine function

The Ferris wheel from the exploration oscillates about 27 m with a deviation of 25 m, and one turn takes 20 minutes. The gondola starts at the bottom and is level with the axle after 5 minutes. With four parameters, $\sin x$ becomes exactly this curve: $h(t) = 25 \cdot \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}(t - 5)\right) + 27$.

KEY POINT · f(x) = a · sin(b(x − c)) + d

$|a|$ is the amplitude (for $a < 0$ reflected in the mean level) · $p = \tfrac{2\pi}{b}$ is the period ($b > 0$)

$c$ shifts to the right (for $x - c$), $d$ upwards: $y = d$ is the mean level, and the values lie between $d - |a|$ and $d + |a|$.

From a measured curve: $d = \tfrac{\max + \min}{2}$, $a = \tfrac{\max - \min}{2}$, $b = \tfrac{2\pi}{p}$, and $c$ is a point at which the curve crosses the mean level rising.

Watch the sign: in $\sin(2(x - 1))$ the shift is 1 to the right, not 2. Factor out first: $\sin(2x - 2) = \sin(2(x - 1))$.

Outlook: an oscillating spring slows down. In a damped oscillation such as $2 \cdot 0.8^t \cdot \sin(2\pi t)$ the amplitude shrinks exponentially, see exercise 17.

INTERACTIVE · SINE WORKSHOP

Change the four parameters one at a time. Dashed: the sine curve $y = \sin x$.

EXAMPLE 5 · THE FERRIS WHEEL AS A FUNCTION

Set up the height $h(t)$ (in m, $t$ in min) of the gondola: axle 27 m, radius 25 m, time for one turn 20 min, getting in at the bottom at $t = 0$.

$d = 27$, $a = 25$, $b = \tfrac{2\pi}{20} = \tfrac{\pi}{10}$. Rising through the mean level after a quarter turn: $c = 5$.

$h(t) = 25\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}(t - 5)\right) + 27$. Check: $h(0) = 2$, $h(10) = 52$.

EXAMPLE 6 · LENGTH OF THE DAY IN DRESDEN

A model: $T(t) = 12.27 + 4.28 \cdot \sin\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{365}(t - 80)\right)$, $t$ the day of the year, $T$ in hours. When is the longest day, and how long is it?

The sine is $1$ when $t - 80$ is a quarter period: $t = 80 + 91.25 = 171.25$, so on 20 or 21 June.

$T = 12.27 + 4.28 = 16.55$ h, that is 16 h 33 min. The shortest day has $7.99$ h, just under 8 hours.

INTERACTIVE · LENGTH OF THE DAY

EXERCISES

Give the amplitude, period and mean level: a) $3\sin x$   b) $\sin(2x)$   c) $2\sin(0.5x) + 1$   d) $-\sin(x - \pi)$

a) 3, $2\pi$, $y = 0$   b) 1, $\pi$, $y = 0$   c) 2, $4\pi$, $y = 1$   d) 1, $2\pi$, $y = 0$. Reflecting and shifting by $\pi$ gives $\sin x$ again.

Which values does $f(x) = 1.5\sin x - 2$ take?

Mean level $-2$, amplitude $1.5$: all values from $-3.5$ to $-0.5$.

Give a sine function with amplitude 2, period $\pi$ and mean level $y = 3$ that passes through the mean level rising at $x = 0$.

$b = \tfrac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2$: $f(x) = 2\sin(2x) + 3$

The mains voltage in Europe can be described by $u(t) = 325\,\text{V} \cdot \sin(2\pi \cdot 50 \cdot t)$ ($t$ in seconds). Give the amplitude, period and frequency. How often per second is the voltage zero?

Amplitude 325 V, $b = 100\pi$, period $\tfrac{2\pi}{100\pi} = 0.02$ s $= 20$ ms, frequency 50 Hz. Two zeros per period: 100 times per second.

Ferris wheel: when is the gondola 40 m high for the first time? For how long per turn is it higher than 40 m?

$\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}(t - 5)\right) = \tfrac{13}{25}$. The graphing calculator gives one solution, the symmetry the second.

$\tfrac{\pi}{10}(t - 5) \approx 0.547$, so $t \approx 6.74$ min. Second solution: $\tfrac{\pi}{10}(t - 5) \approx \pi - 0.547$, $t \approx 13.26$ min. Above 40 m: about 6.5 minutes per turn.

TEST YOURSELF!

The period of $f(x) = 2\sin(0.5x) + 1$ is $k \cdot \pi$. What is $k$?

$\tfrac{2\pi}{0.5} = 4\pi$

What is the mean level of $f(x) = 2\sin(0.5x) + 1$?

$y = d = 1$

Which function has the amplitude 2 and the period $\pi$?

$a = 2$, $b = 2$, $p = \tfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi$

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Fill in the table using the unit circle: $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ for $x = 0$, $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$.

$\sin$: 0, 1, 0, −1, 0 · $\cos$: 1, 0, −1, 0, 1

Connecting with chapter 1.1: a spring oscillates according to $f(t) = 2 \cdot 0.8^t \cdot \sin(2\pi t)$ ($t$ in s). How large is the deviation still after 5 oscillations? After how many seconds has the amplitude fallen below 10% of its initial value?

Amplitude $2 \cdot 0.8^5 \approx 0.66$. $0.8^{10} \approx 0.107$ and $0.8^{11} \approx 0.086$: after 11 seconds.

Day-length model from example 6: on which days is the day as long as the mean level, 12 h 16 min? What is happening in the sky on these days?

At $t = 80$ (21 March) and half a period later at $t = 262.5$ (19 or 20 September): the equinoxes, the beginning of spring and of autumn.

The water level from exercise 3 (between −1.6 m and +1.5 m, period 12.4 h) rises through the mean level at 2:18. Set up a function $h(t)$ ($t$ in hours after midnight). When is high water?

$h(t) = 1.55\sin\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{12.4}(t - 2.3)\right) - 0.05$. High water a quarter period later: $t = 2.3 + 3.1 = 5.4$, so at 5:24, and again at 17:48.

EXCURSIONHISTORY OF SCIENCE

The pharmacist and the sunspots

Heinrich Schwabe was a pharmacist in Dessau and an amateur astronomer. From 1826 he recorded the dark spots on the Sun on every clear day. In fact he was looking for an unknown planet that was supposed to pass between Mercury and the Sun. He never found it. But after 17 years of observation he noticed something else: the number of sunspots rises and falls regularly, with a period of about ten years.

Today this sunspot cycle is known to have a mean period of about 11 years. It is not an exact sine curve; the height and the length of the cycles vary. Even so it matters: when activity is high there are more northern lights, but also more disturbances to satellites and radio.

Source: Heinrich Schwabe: “Sonnen-Beobachtungen im Jahre 1843” (Observations of the Sun in the year 1843), Astronomische Nachrichten 21 (1844), no. 495, cols. 233–236.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

PERIODIC

$f(t + p) = f(t)$, period $p$, frequency $\tfrac1p$. Mean level and amplitude from the largest and the smallest value.

52 m and 2 m: mean level 27 m, amplitude 25 m

RADIANS

$x = \tfrac{\alpha}{180^\circ} \cdot \pi$, one full turn is $2\pi$.

$45^\circ = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$; $2.5 \approx 143.2^\circ$

SINE FUNCTION

Values from $-1$ to $1$, period $2\pi$, zeros $k\pi$, point-symmetric about the origin.

$\sin x = 0.5$: $x = \tfrac{\pi}{6}$ or $\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$

PARAMETERS

$a\sin(b(x - c)) + d$: amplitude $|a|$, period $\tfrac{2\pi}{b}$, $c$ to the right, $d$ upwards.

$h(t) = 25\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}(t - 5)\right) + 27$

MODELLING

From measured data: $d$ and $a$ from the maximum and minimum, $b$ from the period, $c$ where the curve crosses the mean level rising.

Length of the day: longest day 16 h 33 min
